vulnerable_statements.reason: nr_cmds is set before the allocation succeeds. If nvmet_tcp_alloc_cmds() fails, queue->cmds stays NULL while nr_cmds is non-zero. Teardown code such as nvmet_tcp_uninit_data_in_cmds and nvmet_tcp_free_cmds uses nr_cmds to walk queue->cmds, so it dereferences a NULL pointer and crashes the kernel.

The error path does not reset queue->nr_cmds, so the queue stays in an inconsistent state (nr_cmds > 0, cmds == NULL). A remote host can trigger this by sending a Connect with a large queue size that makes the allocation fail.

suggested_fix: Reset the command count when allocation fails, e.g. `if (nvmet_tcp_alloc_cmds(queue)) { queue->nr_cmds = 0; return NVME_SC_INTERNAL; }`. Another option is to set queue->nr_cmds only after the allocation succeeds. Either way, teardown paths never iterate over a NULL cmds array.
